_blame._what: Jas, 2026-10-25: every failure is the worker's output being rejected, the harness failing, or a record that was wrong. This maps the mature four-way taxonomy above onto those words so a count can answer "are the bugs holding the agents back?" without a second vocabulary. EXTERNAL IS KEPT APART on purpose -- collapsing a restart or a disconnect into harness-fault would send a model chasing a bug that does not exist, which is the costliest misattribution this file could make.

_what: The mechanical record of the two schemas Jas ordered 2026-09-20 — how a SCOPE must read a task and how a BRIEF must specify work — grown one entry per MEASURED failure. A failure that is not in this file is one the next scope and brief can repeat; an entry here is one they must address. 'Every failure creates a mechanical part of the schema so there is self improvement and less repetitive failures.'
_grows_by: The coder failure path (t366 build) appends a row mechanically on every failed attempt. A worker session may append with evidence lines. Entries are never deleted; a defense that stops being needed is marked retired with the date, not erased.

_cause_categories._why: The routing decision, made explicit. Until 2026-09-22 only two of these had names — and the one that had none, harness-capability, is where fourteen briefs went wrong: dispatch_loop.futile() had no category for 'the harness could not do it', so it used the one it had and told every future reader the briefs were at fault. A taxonomy with a missing row does not produce a gap, it produces a misfiling. Every entry in `failures` carries a cause_category, and the category decides what happens next WITHOUT anyone reasoning about it.
_cause_categories.content: The scope or the brief is genuinely wrong. Note the reason on the task, move it to the FRONT of the queue, re-scope. The only category where the brief is edited.
_cause_categories.external: Something outside the work ended it — a restart, a disconnect, a machine event. Attribute it, retry ONCE, do not re-scope. The brief was never reached.
_cause_categories.harness-capability: The tooling or the model could not perform the mechanics, independent of what was asked. Repair the harness and re-dispatch the chunk UNCHANGED. Never edit the brief; never retry the same model against the same wall. Added 2026-09-22.
_cause_categories.environment-precondition: A gate refused before any work began — an undeclared red suite, a busy slot, a missing registration. Nothing failed; something was not ready. Satisfy the precondition and re-dispatch. Added 2026-09-22.
_cause_categories.stale-record: The RECORD was wrong and the work may have been fine. Added 2026-10-25 at Jas's "failure classes" instruction: the p487 lane sat 'never closed' for eleven days because its finish rows carried each other's pids; eleven guard-self-test probes sat in the queue after crashed runs; a lane was closed late. The rule: repair the WRITER that made the record wrong, and do not re-dispatch the work -- nothing failed.
_cause_categories._routing_rule: A worker that hits a failure records it and stops; the Manager assigns the category. See docs/skills/root-cause-analysis, Rule 0 — the reporter does not diagnose — and Rule 5 for where the resulting fix lands.
